items.title: 'I cannot teach you integrity': How employee theft is hurting small businesses in Africa
items.summary: Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina shut her waxing studio due to employee theft When popular Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina took a two-week holiday to Europe, she expected to relax. A week into the trip, an Instagram direct message exposed a problem that would ultimately lead to the closure of her business "I was at your studio, I liked everything. The only problem was that I was asked to send money to a different number. It wasn't the number on the wall," a customer wrote to her Boina had opened Waxaholic Studio, a waxing and hydrafacial parlour in Nairobi's central business district, on 1 September 2024. A year later, she had hired a receptionist and two specialists and felt confident enough to take a two-week holiday, her first international trip of the year "I trusted them. It's two rooms and a reception - how do you mess that up?" she recalls thinking "It never occurred to me that maybe I was getting clients and someone else was stealing from me," she tells the BBC The discovery prompted Boina to examine the business more closely.

items.title: Nigeria: Tinubu launches reelection bid amid economic woes
items.summary: President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation Nigeria 's President Bola Tinubu on Saturday formally launched his campaign for a second term "We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity," Tinubu said at a rally in the northwestern state of Kaduna "You grant me the privilege to promise you once again, there is that promise of a better tomorrow," he added Africa's most populous country will hold its next presidential election in January 2027 . items.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. items.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
items.summary: File image of Nigerian police officers Unknown gunmen have raided a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say There are fears the actual death toll is much higher, with eyewitnesses speaking of 20 lives lost and a non-governmental organisation suggesting a toll of as many as 50 The gunmen reportedly swooped on the village of Binnari in the Karim Lamido area mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday in a rampage that went on for up to four hours Police say they are searching for other casualties in the bush but the authorities were accused by Amnesty International of failing to protect rural communities Nigeria continues to face attacks by armed groups across several regions, including the northwest, northeast and central regions The country is also battling a jihadist insurgency in its north-east that has lasted nearly two decades, drawing persistent criticism of the government's handling of insecurity Following the latest incident, police said they recovered…

items.title: Mozambique: Govt plans 5,541 new civil service hires in 2027, with a budget impact of 1.399 billion meticais
items.summary: According to data from the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (Plano Económico e Social e Orçamento do Estado – PESOE) compiled today by Lusa, the number of new recruits projected for 2027 represents an increase of 39.9% compared with the 3,962 admissions projected for 2026, while the corresponding budget impact rises by 23.3%, from 1.135 billion meticais (€15.9 million) budgeted for this year to 1.399 billion meticais (€19.6 million) in 2027 Education will continue to account for the largest share of recruitment, with 2,978 admissions planned, equivalent to 53.7% of the total, mainly involving general education teachers. In this sector, the estimated budget impact amounts to 903 million meticais (€12.6 million), corresponding to around two-thirds of the total cost of new admissions planned for next year The proposal also provides for the recruitment of 1,364 employees for the Justice Administration bodies, more than double the 745 admissions planned for 2026.
